chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl bin Ziyad, from Ali bin Asbaat, from Ismail bin Yasar, from someone who reported it, said:

He said: When a matter grieves you, so say at the end of your prostration (sujood), 'O Jibraeel! O Muhammad! O Jibraeel! O Muhammad!', repeating that, 'Suffice me for what I am in, for both of you are sufficing ones, and protect me by the Permission of Allah, for both of you are protectors'.
ai.seo_question: What is the supplication for distress and grief in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: This supplication, found in al-Kafi, emphasizes the intercessory role of the Prophet Muhammad and the Archangel Jibraeel as mediators of divine relief during times of distress. By invoking them in the final prostration, the supplicant acknowledges their status as 'kafi' (sufficient) and 'hafiz' (protector) by God's permission, reflecting the Shia belief in the spiritual authority of the Ahl al-Bayt and their angels. This practice highlights the theological concept of seeking closeness to God through the beloved figures of the faith during moments of vulnerability.
